title: Storage
description: Storage trends: used/free per disk, forecast, size per media category, retention. Docker/grafana/README.md 'Storage trends'.

panels.title: Now (used of size; free = until each disk's limit)
beefy SSD · limit 80 %
panels.description: Both SSDs of beefy's hot tier, where downloads land. Yellow from 70 % (mover starts), orange from 75 %, red at the 80 % limit. Limits (never filled to 100 %): SSD 80 % = mergerfs keeps 1479G free per SSD, new downloads then go to the HDD (the nightly mover starts at 70 % and moves down to 60 %); HDD 90 % = 2800G kept free, Radarr/Sonarr stop importing; audiobook disk 80 % (red on the audiobook bar; nothing stops writes, the fastpi disk alert fires at 85 %). Source: homelab:storage_* (rules/storage-trends.yml).

panels.title: beefy HDD · limit 90 %
panels.description: beefy's archive HDD. Yellow from 80 % (BeefyHddFilling), orange from 85 %, red at the 90 % limit. Limits (never filled to 100 %): SSD 80 % = mergerfs keeps 1479G free per SSD, new downloads then go to the HDD (the nightly mover starts at 70 % and moves down to 60 %); HDD 90 % = 2800G kept free, Radarr/Sonarr stop importing; audiobook disk 80 % (red on the audiobook bar; nothing stops writes, the fastpi disk alert fires at 85 %). Source: homelab:storage_* (rules/storage-trends.yml).

panels.title: Audiobook disk (fastpi) · limit 80 %
panels.description: fastpi's /mnt/seagate-black: audiobooks and podcasts, used as df counts it (ext4 reserve left out). Orange from 70 %, red at 80 % (audiobook bar colours). Limits (never filled to 100 %): SSD 80 % = mergerfs keeps 1479G free per SSD, new downloads then go to the HDD (the nightly mover starts at 70 % and moves down to 60 %); HDD 90 % = 2800G kept free, Radarr/Sonarr stop importing; audiobook disk 80 % (red on the audiobook bar; nothing stops writes, the fastpi disk alert fires at 85 %). Source: homelab:storage_* (rules/storage-trends.yml).

panels.title: Total combined · limit usable
panels.description: All three disks against their usable space (each disk's size x its limit), so 100 % = every disk at its limit. Limits (never filled to 100 %): SSD 80 % = mergerfs keeps 1479G free per SSD, new downloads then go to the HDD (the nightly mover starts at 70 % and moves down to 60 %); HDD 90 % = 2800G kept free, Radarr/Sonarr stop importing; audiobook disk 80 % (red on the audiobook bar; nothing stops writes, the fastpi disk alert fires at 85 %). Source: homelab:storage_* (rules/storage-trends.yml).

panels.title: Limit reached in ~ (estimate)
panels.description: Days until each disk reaches its limit (not 100 %) if it keeps filling like in the last 30 days: where predict_linear's line of free space reaches the limit's reserve (1 h steps). SSD also: days until the nightly mover starts (70 %). An estimate: one big download, the mover or a delete changes it. Limits (never filled to 100 %): SSD 80 % = mergerfs keeps 1479G free per SSD, new downloads then go to the HDD (the nightly mover starts at 70 % and moves down to 60 %); HDD 90 % = 2800G kept free, Radarr/Sonarr stop importing; audiobook disk 80 % (red on the audiobook bar; nothing stops writes, the fastpi disk alert fires at 85 %).

panels.title: Growth per month (estimate)
panels.description: How much more is used per 30 days at the pace of the last 30 days (negative: shrinking). Same fit as "Limit reached in".

panels.title: Total combined
panels.description: All three disks against their usable space (each disk's size x its limit), so 100 % = every disk at its limit. Dashed: size (grey), limit (red).

panels.title: Size per category (stacked)
panels.description: Films and series from beefy's Radarr/Sonarr file records (beefy_library_bytes, hourly while beefy is awake, kept while it sleeps); quality 4K HDR = 2160p with HDR/Dolby Vision, 720p/other = everything below 1080p. Audiobooks, podcasts, ebooks, music: folder sizes on fastpi (fastpi_library_bytes, daily 05:17). A category without a library has no line.

panels.title: Size now
panels.description: Last value per category; ebooks and music show "no library yet" until a folder for them is listed in library-exporter/libraries.toml and exists.

panels.title: Titles now
panels.description: Films: one per film. Series: one per series, counted under the quality holding most of its bytes. Audiobooks/podcasts: folders holding files (CD/Disc folders count as one).

panels.title: Kept forever
panels.description: Titles the retention rules keep (old, niche, highly rated, Keep forever choices, protected): beefy_retention_bytes{state="keep"}.

panels.title: Temporary (would be freed)
panels.description: Titles the rules would delete once their time is up: the space deletion frees over time. Deletion is off while retention runs in observe mode.

panels.title: Leaving within 7 days
panels.description: Temporary titles whose delete date is at most 7 days away.
